Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL-prime-agent-luna6-medium-ws0/frozen/held-out-2/play/users/u041/system/state/workspace/programs/task-d63fb094.py')
p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
code='''def transform(grid):
    sep = next(r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if row and all(v == 5 for v in row))
    above = [(r, c, grid[r][c]) for r in range(sep) for c in range(len(grid[r])) if grid[r][c] not in (0, 5)]
    right_color = max(above, key=lambda p: p[1])[2]
    top_cells = [(r, c) for r, c, color in above if color == right_color]
    top_min_r = min(r for r, c in top_cells)
    top_min_c = min(c for r, c in top_cells)
    lower_cells = [(r, c) for r in range(sep + 1, len(grid)) for c, color in enumerate(grid[r]) if color not in (0, 5)]
    lower_min_r = min(r for r, c in lower_cells)
    lower_min_c = min(c for r, c in lower_cells)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid[sep + 1:]]
    top_h = max(r for r, c in top_cells) - top_min_r + 1
    for r, c in top_cells:
        rr = lower_min_r - (sep + 1) - top_h + (r - top_min_r)
        cc = lower_min_c + (c - top_min_c)
        out[rr][cc] = right_color
    return out
'''
p.write_text(code)
